description:
We’re a team of four from Kamloops, BC, taking on the “Space Mission Design Game” challenge. We’re building a swipe-based card game where students run a space outpost and every decision shifts their power, food, shielding and life support, so they learn how hard it is to keep a crew alive.

Our strengths are software and web development. We’d welcome anyone with an eye for art, game design or space science.
summary: Outpost Trainer is our team's browser card game for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 ("Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer"), built in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Players run a lunar outpost by swiping cards left or right, balancing four meters: Power, Food, Shield and Life. The game follows five main story quests: mission design, a colony upgrade, a crisis shaped by that upgrade, a cavern expansion, and building a landing pad. Rover and alien side quests are woven in. Choices draw on real NASA missions and technology such as VIPER, Kilopower and the Lunar Gateway. As players progress, their base grows on the Moon in the background: the outpost, rover, alien saucer and branch-specific upgrades. Previews hint which meters a choice affects, low meters pulse red, and a cargo landing marks victory. We balanced it to about a 44% win rate for a typical player.
details:
Outpost Trainer is a browser card game that puts players in charge of a lunar outpost. Each card presents a real mission situation with two choices, and players swipe left or right (or use the arrow keys) to decide. Every choice changes four survival meters: Power, Food, Shield and Life. If any meter hits zero, the mission fails. Players progress through five main story quests: designing the mission, upgrading the colony, surviving a crisis shaped by their earlier choices, expanding into a lunar cavern, and building a landing pad for Earth’s cargo ship, which is the win condition. Rover and alien side quests appear along the way. As players progress, their base visibly grows on the Moon behind the cards, with an outpost, a rover and upgrades that match the paths they chose.


The game teaches the trade-offs real mission planners face: every decision has a cost, and there’s rarely a perfect answer. It runs in any web browser with no installation, account or download, so it works in classrooms, at home and on phones. A full game takes about 10–15 minutes.


We want to spark interest in space exploration among young future astronauts by showing that living on the Moon means balancing energy, food, radiation protection and crew health. The cards are grounded in real NASA missions and technology, including VIPER, Kilopower, Veggie, the Lunar Gateway, SLS, Apollo 13, Surveyor 3, Astrobee, Valkyrie, SPLICE, Whipple shields and Shackleton Crater, so players learn real science while they play.
